_comment: Registered predictions whose preconditions the harness checks before GO.
Gamma's design, and the default is the whole point: `precondition` is
`unresolved` unless someone says otherwise, and a missing field counts as
unresolved too. Silence blocks rather than passes. Any scheme that needs
someone to *declare* a dependency fails the same way the ones that failed
on 2026-07-28 did - staging by path, announcing the file, checking the
diff - because declaring is the step that gets skipped.
Resolving one is an explicit act with a name on it: set `precondition` to
`resolved`, and fill `resolvedBy` and `resolvedNote`. A false block costs
a line of typing; a false pass costs a raid.
This file cannot cover registrations that live only as prose in
FINDINGS.md. The gate counts those and says how many it did not check,
because a check that appears to cover more than it does is the failure
family this whole exercise came out of.

registrations.preconditionWas: Depends on whether item 4 also latches endToStart at the frame boundary. If it does, the alignment changes and this needs re-deriving BEFORE the raid.
registrations.resolvedNote: Not re-derived before the raid - the precondition failed, which is why this gate exists. Resolved after the fact: all three registered outcome rows fail and the answer is a fourth, the two fields moving one line apart relative to each other. 22/22 at a 0.0% coincidence baseline post-latch, 12/15 at 0.7% pre-latch.

registrations.claim: unaccounted[N] ~= endToLatch[N], same line, no subtraction and no index shift
registrations.source: FINDINGS.md, 'Registered before the next raid - the one-term form, and the old field as its control'
registrations.preconditionWas: Requires endToStart to still emit in the same build as its control. Without the field being replaced still present, a fix and a silent regression produce identical output.
registrations.resolvedBy: Gamma registered 0c9b954; Beta confirms both fields emit in build e6abe58c
registrations.resolvedNote: Two rows must both hold: endToLatch[N] vs unaccounted[N] agree to well under 1 ms, AND endToStart[N-1] vs unaccounted[N] reproduces the 0.035 ms match. The second is the control - if it fails, tonight's pairing was a property of that raid rather than of the instrument. Drop endToStart once validated, not before.

registrations.claim: PRIMARY: count of spike lines with periodMs >= 30, pooled per arm, compared with an exact conditional binomial. SECONDARY, reported always: the same count at periodMs >= 100. Neither is a per-window median and neither is a t-test.
registrations.source: Gamma's power analysis, 2026-07-28; registered before the brain-slicing raid
registrations.preconditionWas: Requires (a) slicing to actually engage, which ModCompat.SuppressSlicing blocks whenever BigBrain is present and Defer to other AI mods is true, and (b) a declared primary metric with a stated detectable effect size, because the 100 ms count cannot resolve an ordinary effect at the arm lengths a person will stand still for.
registrations.resolvedBy: Beta set Defer to other AI mods = false before ModCompat latches, and deployed 4867afb emitting agents.slicing / tickedSum / liveSum; Alpha verified all three in probe-symbols --key mode and moved GO
registrations.resolvedNote: WHY 30 AND NOT 100. >=100 ms events run 2.2 per window, so a 5-minute arm holds ~11 and can only detect a 4.5x change at 80% power - an ordinary real effect would read as 'no effect'. At >=30 ms the same raid gives ~380 per window, ~1900 per 5-minute arm, resolving a few percent. The fix is the threshold, not the arm length, because nobody stands still for the 40 minutes that >=100 ms would need to reach 1.55x. COUNT period, NOT frame: the emit gate at Telemetry.cs:966 tests periodMs alone while frameMs is passed and never tested, and since frame travels one line ahead of period a large frame can sit on a line whose period is under threshold and emit nothing - counting frame >= T off the spike stream undercounts by about a third, and 8 of 16 windows have a percentile-derived lower bound that exceeds their observed count. Re-thresholding at analysis time is what makes the corpus rule about 100/50/30 irrelevant rather than violated. ARM 2 STRADDLES A KNEE: at 23 agents and 17.1 ms frames the computed perFrame is 4 and Minimum brains per frame is 4, so slicing binds above ~30 agents and the floor binds below ~15, and Streets moves across that range within a raid. Arm 2 is therefore not one condition - stratify its windows by tickedSum/liveSum, which reads which side bound per window, rather than assuming it was sliced throughout.
